annotations.title: Which businesses make up this industry here, and how big are they?

description: Use when the user is sizing a B2B market in firms, planning a roll-up or territory, or asks how many companies of a kind exist: "how many CPA firms are in Texas?", "how many restaurants are in Harris County, and how big are they?". Returns employer establishments, employees and payroll from County Business Patterns, the split by employee size, and solo businesses with no payroll from Nonemployer Statistics. Refuses before you are charged if the code matches nothing or the size classes do not add up. Every result carries a run id, a date and a citation line. Calling this tool returns a quote, not the result: what the run measures, its price and a payment_url. The run happens only when you POST to payment_url, and a run that fails its controls refuses there with nothing charged. Dimensions (vary these inputs to cut the answer; each call is its own run): over time: one release (latest County Business Patterns and Nonemployer year); place: state, county, cbsa or zip; segment: naics; size class (in the result). Price: $0.05 per run over x402 (USDC on Base, no account needed), or $0.50 over MPP (a Stripe shared payment token); charged only when the run comes back sound. For how many people hold the buyer’s job in the area, use run_buyer_roles.
